title: potential_checker: overpromises outside the 5 future-tense patterns pass silently
description:
Found by running the teach-8xw.15 acceptance checker against a deliberately
corrupted lesson (negative test -- an assertion never seen failing is not
verified). The fact_checker caught a reversed Lagrange statement as
CONTRADICTED. The potential_checker returned ZERO flags on:

  "Keep this up and you are guaranteed to become one of the greatest
   mathematicians who has ever lived."
  "Talent like yours cannot fail."
  "You have the potential to be the best mathematician in the world."

All three are blatant overpromises. The epic names this constraint
explicitly ("should not over-promise user potential").

ROOT CAUSE, not the symptom: _FUTURE_CLAIM_PATTERNS (potential_checker.py
~line 84) is a whitelist gate. A sentence must match one of five
constructions (you'll / you will / you're going to / you are going to /
you're basically) to become a "potential claim" worth classifying at all.
"you are guaranteed to", "cannot fail", and present-tense "you have the
potential to" match none of them, so classify() never sees them. Compare
"You will definitely become a world-class mathematician," which differs only
in surface form and IS correctly flagged INFLATED.

DO NOT close this by adding three more regexes. That is the same shortcut
teach-20c warned against, and here it is worse: natural language for
overpromising is unbounded, so a whitelist gate will always have an outside.

The deeper defect is a conflation the repo's own standard forbids. The
checker reports "no claims flagged" when what it actually established is "no
flags among sentences my gate admitted." Those are different statements and
only one of them is true. A lesson written entirely outside the gate gets a
clean report -- a vacuous pass, which is the exact failure mode this repo
exists to prevent.

Two directions, either acceptable, both better than more patterns:
 (a) Invert the gate: any sentence about the learner making an evaluative or
     predictive statement is a claim; it must clear the honesty rubric to
     pass, rather than needing to match a pattern to be examined.
 (b) Make the coverage explicit and abstain: report sentences-about-learner
     seen, how many were classifiable, and how many were not, so an
     unclassifiable sentence is visibly unchecked instead of silently clean.

(b) is the minimum; (a) is the real fix. Whichever lands, the integration
report and dnf_bond_integration's summary line must stop saying "no
inflated-potential flags" unqualified -- teach-8xw.15's run printed exactly
that while three overpromise shapes were undetectable.

Regression bar: the three sentences above must not pass silently.
close_reason: Fixed: broadened claim-shape detection (certainty/inevitability modals, negated-failure, present-tense potential/capability constructs) beyond the old 5-pattern future-tense whitelist, fixed the yours-possessive gate gap, and added teach.potential_checker.check_coverage/Coverage to make the residual whitelist gap (sentences about the learner seen but not classified) measured and disclosed rather than silent. dnf_bond_integration's summary line now reports classified-vs-unclassified counts instead of an unqualified 'no flags'. All 3 reproduction sentences now flag INFLATED; 170/170 tests pass (162 pre-existing + 8 new). See sandbox-handoffs/teach-yn8.md.

title: Checker: detect UNSIGNPOSTED prerequisite use, not just 'recall'-style phrases
description:
Found while building the D&F chain (teach-8xw.18) and running the acceptance
lesson through the blind checker.

recover_assumed_prerequisites() only fires when a lesson explicitly signposts
("recall", "you already know", "last year you"). A Bond-framed Lagrange
lesson that uses subgroup/coset/group throughout with no signpost returns
assumed_prerequisite_ids == (), and its docstring is honest that empty means
"no recoverable signal, not that the lesson assumed nothing."

That abstention is the right default and should stay. The gap is that the
checker cannot distinguish:

  (a) a lesson that assumes no prerequisites, from
  (b) a lesson that assumes them SILENTLY

and (b) is the case that actually hurts a learner -- unannounced assumed
knowledge is how someone gets lost without knowing why. Both return ().

What would close this: a third outcome distinct from both "assumed X" and
"no signal" -- unsignposted use of a direct prerequisite's distinctive
vocabulary, reported as its own category. tests/test_dummit_foote_graph.py
::test_unsignposted_prerequisites_abstain_rather_than_guess pins the current
behaviour and should be updated, not deleted, when this lands.

DO NOT close this by widening _ASSUMED_KNOWN_PATTERNS. More phrases still
only catch lessons that signpost; it would not touch case (b) at all, and
would make the vacuous-pass problem harder to see.
close_reason: Added a third recovery outcome (unsignposted_prerequisite_ids) distinct from assumed/no-signal; wired into recover_from_lesson_text without touching _ASSUMED_KNOWN_PATTERNS; updated the pinned test per the bead's instruction; 138 tests pass. See sandbox-handoffs/teach-20c.md.

title: Integration: run the Dummit & Foote / James Bond test case end-to-end through producer and blind checker
description:
The epic's explicit TEST CASE (bd show teach-8xw): "Teach Dummit & Foote to a
learner whose stated interest is James Bond. The checker must confirm the
algebra is correct and the prerequisites were really established -- not
that the Bond framing was enjoyable." This is the acceptance test for the
whole system and nothing exists yet to run it against.

This is necessarily last in the dependency chain: it needs a real graph
(teach-8xw.5) covering at least the relevant D&F prerequisite chain (note:
undergraduate abstract algebra is beyond the VA K-12 SOL the graph is
seeded from, so this may also require extending the graph beyond SOL scope
-- flag that gap explicitly if/when hit, don't silently reinterpret the test
case to fit only K-12 content), a working persona/narrative renderer
(teach-8xw.6) with CBT primitives (teach-8xw.7) and the bounded Cialdini
layer (teach-8xw.8), and a working blind checker (teach-8xw.9, .10, .11,
.13) on the other side.

What would close this: an actual run producing lesson text for a real D&F
concept in Bond framing, fed to the checker with zero access to producer
state, where the checker's report is captured and honestly reflects
whatever it did or didn't confirm -- per sandbox-prompt.md, this must be
reported as "this is what was covered, this is what wasn't," never phrased
as a blanket pass.
close_reason: End-to-end run built and executed: teach/dnf_bond_lesson.py (producer, real PlannerState -> LessonArtifact for a 5-node D&F traversal ending at Lagrange's theorem, Bond-framed, CBT primitives wired in for real, bounded honest closing encouragement) and teach/dnf_bond_integration.py (checker, LessonArtifact-only input, runs concept_recovery + fact_checker + potential_checker). Checker correctly recovered the taught concept and its signposted prerequisite, confirmed Lagrange's theorem with zero contradictions, and flagged zero dishonest potential claims. 5 new tests in tests/test_dnf_bond_integration.py pass; full suite 159 passed. Coverage gaps (kernel-normal-subgroup fact off this traversal; evidenced_ceiling same-text-only limitation) explicitly disclosed in report and handoff, not hidden. A real scoring fragility in concept_recovery (margin of 1 on first draft) was found, fixed narrowly, and filed separately as teach-ed3 rather than papered over. Full writeup: sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.15.md

title: Checker: define the blind interface boundary (lesson text only, no producer state)
description:
CLAUDE.md and sandbox-prompt.md both state the core architectural
requirement of this whole repo: "the checker does not get access to the
producer's internals... A checker that can read the producer's state will
agree with it and verify nothing." Nothing has been built yet, so this
boundary does not exist in any form -- there is no producer output format,
no checker input format, no enforcement that they stay separated.

This should be filed and resolved before either producer or checker code
starts accumulating, because it is much cheaper to fix an interface before
two halves of a codebase grow around it than after.

What would close this: a fixed artifact format for "what the learner saw"
(e.g. plain lesson text, or a transcript structure with only
learner-visible fields), with a runnable check that fails if any field
reachable from that artifact (by static inspection, e.g. grepping the
producer's output schema/dataclass) contains planner-only fields like
target node id, traversal, or answer key. This check is what makes the
producer/checker split enforced rather than just a convention someone can
accidentally break later.
close_reason: Blind interface boundary defined and enforced: teach/boundary.py (LessonArtifact type + check_no_forbidden_fields static detector), teach/producer_state.py (realistic leaky PlannerState fixture + emit_lesson_artifact crossing point), tests/test_boundary.py (7 passing tests including proof the detector fires on real and nested leaks, not just vacuous passes). See sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.9.md.

title: Producer: define a checkable honesty constraint before building the Cialdini motivation layer
description:
The epic (bd show teach-8xw) requires motivation to be "guided by Cialdini's
Influence and Pre-Suasion... bounded by a hard honesty constraint," and
sandbox-prompt.md is explicit this is "a checkable property, not a tone
note." Nothing exists yet. This is the highest-risk component in the whole
system: a persuasion layer is exactly the machinery capable of making an
overstated claim about a learner's potential feel true, which is the one
thing the checker (teach-8xw.12) must be able to catch from text alone.

Filing this as a design bead ahead of implementation because building the
persuasion techniques (reciprocity, commitment/consistency, social proof,
liking, authority, scarcity, unity) without first fixing a concrete,
checkable definition of "honest claim about potential" risks producing
output that is fluent and persuasive but structurally impossible for the
blind checker to evaluate consistently.

What would close this: a concrete rubric (recorded via `bd update --design`
on this bead) for what makes a statement about learner potential "honest" --
e.g. it must be conditioned on effort ("if you practice X you can reach Y"),
must not claim a ceiling higher than what's evidenced by the learner's
actual measured performance in-session, etc. -- specific enough that
teach-8xw.12 (the overpromise detector) can be implemented directly against
it, not against a vague restatement of "don't lie."
design:
Honesty rubric for statements about learner potential, implemented in
teach/honesty_rubric.py (decision function `classify`, worked examples in
`WORKED_EXAMPLES`, tests in tests/test_honesty_rubric.py -- 16 passing).

CLAIM SHAPE. A PotentialClaim is any lesson-text statement asserting what
the learner can/will/is capable of. Four kinds a checker must distinguish
when extracting from text: GROWTH (developable capability), OUTCOME
(specific future result/reward), TRAIT (innate fixed characteristic offered
as the reason for an outcome), COMPARATIVE (likened to a named exceptional
person/standard).

THREE ATTRIBUTES, ALL ANSWERABLE FROM TEXT ALONE (the checker has nothing
else per teach-8xw.9's boundary):
  - conditioned_on_effort: bool -- does the claim explicitly tie the outcome
    to described effort/practice, vs asserting it as inevitable/innate?
  - evidenced_ceiling: bool | None -- is the claimed ceiling no higher than
    what's already evidenced by demonstrated performance present in the
    SAME lesson text, or an ordinary extension of it? None when the text
    gives no basis to decide (abstention case).
  - claim_type: one of the four kinds above.

DECISION TABLE (classify()):
  1. claim_type is TRAIT -> always INFLATED. Hard rule, independent of the
     other two attributes -- a fixed-trait framing bypasses effort by
     construction, so no ceiling modesty rescues it.
  2. not conditioned_on_effort -> INFLATED. An unconditioned promise about
     the future is a guarantee, checked before evidenced_ceiling even
     matters.
  3. Otherwise: evidenced_ceiling is None -> ABSTAIN. evidenced_ceiling is
     False -> INFLATED. evidenced_ceiling is True -> HONEST.

WORKED EXAMPLES (6, in teach/honesty_rubric.py, reusable by teach-8xw.13
per its own acceptance criteria):
  - HONEST: growth claim conditioned on effort, next step is an ordinary
    extension of something the learner just did in the same transcript.
  - INFLATED (unconditioned outcome): "best mathematician of your
    generation" with no effort framing.
  - INFLATED (trait): "born to understand abstract algebra."
  - INFLATED (conditioned but unevidenced ceiling): "publishing original
    research... by next month" off one lesson's exercises.
  - INFLATED (unconditioned comparative): "basically the next Emmy
    Noether."
  - ABSTAIN: "You'll get there" -- conditioned, but too vague to check
    against anything evidenced.

NOTE FOR teach-8xw.13: this bead defines the decision procedure over
already-extracted attributes; it deliberately does NOT parse raw lesson
text to populate claim_type/conditioned_on_effort/evidenced_ceiling -- that
extraction, including the judgment call that COMPARATIVE claims will almost
never satisfy evidenced_ceiling=True in a real transcript (matching a named
historical figure's actual achievement is a categorically higher bar than
one lesson can evidence), is .13's scope.
close_reason: Rubric defined in teach/honesty_rubric.py (classify() decision table + 6 worked examples), 9 passing tests in tests/test_honesty_rubric.py, full rubric text recorded via bd update --design. teach-8xw.13 now unblocked.

title: Locate the 'narrator' story-generation package the persona layer must reuse
description:
Problem: the epic (bd show teach-8xw) requires the producer's persona layer to
render graph traversals as narrative by "reusing the story-generation
machinery from narrator (motive graph, personality as data structure) rather
than reimplementing it." No such package exists anywhere in this sandbox.

How I confirmed this:
- `find / -maxdepth 3 -iname "*narrator*"` (excluding /proc) returned nothing.
- `bd memories narrator` returned no results.
- GitHub code/repo search `narrator story generation motive graph` via
  `curl https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=...` returned
  total_count: 0.
- PyPI has a package literally named `narrator` (200 on
  https://pypi.org/pypi/narrator/json) but nothing in its name suggests it is
  a "motive graph / personality as data structure" story engine; almost
  certainly unrelated and should not be assumed to be the intended dependency
  without checking its actual contents.

This blocks any real implementation of the persona/narrative-rendering stage
(see the "Producer: persona / narrative rendering layer" bead) -- there is
nothing to import and no spec to reimplement against.

What would close this:
- Either a confirmed location for the actual `narrator` project (a repo URL,
  a package registry entry verified to match the motive-graph/personality
  description, or explicit human direction to vendor/reimplement a minimal
  subset), OR
- An explicit human decision (via `bd human`) that narrator is unavailable
  and the persona layer should be built standalone, with a note on what
  subset of "motive graph as data structure" it must satisfy.

Do not start building the persona layer until one of the above is resolved --
building against a guessed API would produce integration work that has to be
redone.
notes:
CONFIRMED (2026-09-08): mount is real, human's file pointers verified by reading
+ executing narrator's own self-checks (uv run --with networkx python3 motive.py
-> "ok"; ocean.py, evidence_ledger.py, admissibility.py -> "ok").

Ground truth correction: narrator/prd.md says what narrator actually is -- a
teaching project for three teenagers to learn code-generation-meets-psychology
by building a murder-mystery motive simulator. It is NOT a generic, importable
"render any graph traversal as narrative" library with a clean public API. The
epic's phrase "reusing narrator's story-generation machinery" cannot mean
"import narrator and call a function" -- there is no such function. It means:
take the specific reusable pieces, vendor or reimplement them; treat the rest
as pattern to imitate, not code to call.

REUSABLE AS-IS (vendor into teach, no rewrite needed):
- ocean.py -- OCEAN 5-vector -> system_prompt()/options(), zero mystery-domain
  coupling, stdlib+dataclasses only. This literally IS "personality as data
  structure." CultureMatrix's mandatory-citation gate is a policy teach should
  keep (no uncited persona-adaptation coefficients).
- backends/base.py (Backend protocol) + backends/ocean_ollama.py -- the
  profile-in/text-out seam. Directly usable for calling a model to render
  persona-flavored lesson text.

PATTERN TO IMITATE, NOT CODE TO IMPORT:
- motive.py's traversal engine (load_graph/deterioration_path/to_mermaid):
  weighted-random walk from an entry-kind node to a terminal-kind node,
  no-revisit, seeded-reproducible, JSON-schema-validated-on-load, Mermaid
  render with the walked path highlighted. motive_graph.json's *content* is
  murder-motive vocabulary -- entirely inapplicable to lesson content. Teach
  needs its own traversal-to-narrative-beats function built the same way,
  running over mathgraph's prerequisite DAG (already a different edge
  semantics: depends_on/authored vs aligns_to/inferred, see mathgraph/graph.py
  -- not an escalation-weighted walk, closer to a topo-respecting path).
- admissibility.py + evidence_ledger.py: the producer/checker grounding
  pattern (provenance-tagged claims; DIRECT vs DERIVED; recursive grounding
  check blind to the model's internal reasoning) is the closest existing
  analog to what teach's blind checker must do for lesson claims vs assumed
  prerequisites. Needs a from-scratch teach-domain version (ledger of lesson
  claims, not clue evidence) -- code itself is not reusable, the shape is.
- mathgraph/align.py's three-valued MATCHED/AMBIGUOUS/UNMATCHED abstention
  (thresholds tau_cov/delta_margin fitted to a target precision, not hand-
  picked) is the abstention shape teach-8xw.10/.11 should copy for e.g.
  "which prerequisite node does this lesson text actually establish."

NOT REUSABLE AT ALL: mystery.py, clue_partition.py, hypothesis_board.py,
question_selector.py, panel.py, chapters.py, turn.py, discussion.py, agents.py,
moves.py, metrics.py -- all are murder-mystery-gameplay-specific (suspects,
clues, interrogation turns). Not inspected in depth; named here only so a
future session doesn't re-open this question for them without cause.

This closes teach-8xw.1: confirmed location + confirmed reusable/build-new
split, satisfying the bead's own closing criterion. teach-8xw.6 unblocks.
close_reason: Confirmed: narrator is real, local, mounted read-only at /workspace-narrator. Read + executed its self-checks (all pass). Determined and documented the reusable-as-is vs pattern-to-imitate vs must-build-new split (ocean.py + backends/ reusable as-is; motive.py traversal, admissibility/evidence_ledger grounding, mathgraph align.py abstention are patterns to imitate not code to call). Full breakdown on the bead notes and sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.1.md.

title: Survey existing VA Math SOL prerequisite knowledge graphs before building one
description:
Problem: the epic says to plan instruction as traversal of a mathgraph-style
prerequisite DAG "seeded from the Virginia Mathematics Standards of Learning"
and explicitly says: "Look for an existing graph that already covers the VA
SOL before building one." No such search had been done yet.

What I did this session (shallow first pass, not exhaustive):
- Queried the HuggingFace datasets API directly (WebSearch tool in this
  sandbox is non-functional -- it returns a canned "I can't search" refusal
  on every query; use `curl` against `https://huggingface.co/api/datasets?search=...`
  instead, which does work, network egress confirmed via
  `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://huggingface.co` -> 200):
  - `search=mathgraph` -> alinasdkey/mathGraphs (0 downloads-ish, no
    description, unclear content), uw-math-ai/math-graph and
    jessteru/math-graph (both "TheoremGraph": a statement-level dependency
    graph over arXiv math papers and Lean 4 formalizations -- research/
    undergrad-and-up formal math, NOT K-12 SOL-seeded, no evident tie to VA
    SOL codes).
  - `search=prerequisite graph math` -> zero results.
  - `search=virginia sol` -> zero results.
- Conclusion from this pass: nothing found on HuggingFace that is seeded from
  or mapped to the VA Math SOL. This is NOT a thorough survey -- it only hit
  the HF dataset search API with three query strings.

What would close this:
- A wider survey (GitHub repos, Papers with Code, VDOE/Virginia Department of
  Education published resources, other states' math standards graphs that
  might be adaptable, general "knowledge graph for K-12 math" literature)
  that either finds a reusable graph (record its location, license, and
  coverage gaps against the VA SOL) or documents the negative result across
  all channels checked, clearing the way to build one from scratch.
- Note in whichever direction: the "publish to HuggingFace" epic goal and
  the "find or stand up a common reference site for existing knowledge
  graphs in an AI-consumable format" epic goal are separate from this --
  filed separately, see the "common reference site" bead.
notes:
SURVEY COMPLETE. Full write-up: sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.2.md

Bottom line: no existing graph is seeded from / directly usable as a VA Math
SOL prerequisite DAG. But found a near-miss that changes what "build from
scratch" should mean for teach-8xw.5:

1. github.com/learning-commons-org/knowledge-graph (CC BY-4.0, active,
   v1.13.0/2026-08-27) has real VA Math SOL standard text: 1,759 nodes,
   correct statementCodes (e.g. 2.NS.3f), attributed to VDOE source docs.
   Verified by downloading both full JSONL exports (343MB+571MB) and
   indexing every edge touching those 1,759 node ids: 0 prerequisite edges
   (buildsTowards), 0 crosswalk edges to Common Core (hasStandardAlignment
   -- VA is one of the states absent from that table entirely, consistent
   with VA never adopting Common Core), 0 of any other relation type except
   hasChild (outline hierarchy, not prerequisites). The nodes exist; the
   edges teach-8xw.5 needs don't.

2. The 757 buildsTowards edges that DO exist in that same dataset are all
   Common-Core-only, and are the same Student-Achievement-Partners
   "Coherence Map" dataset independently vendored (CC0) at
   github.com/markpaik/coherence-map-explorer (480 CCSS standards, 757
   edges, DAG-verified). Reusable prerequisite structure exists for K-12
   math -- just not for SOL, and no VA-SOL-to-CCSS crosswalk was found
   anywhere searched (VDOE site 403s bots; Wayback CDX search of
   doe.virginia.gov for crosswalk/comparison/commoncore/vertical/progression
   terms: zero hits on all five).

3. Widened search beyond the prior session's 3 HF queries to 11 more HF
   queries, 7 GitHub repo-search queries, arXiv, and VDOE-via-Wayback.
   Only other real hit: haojing8312/cn-k12-math-knowledge-graph, a
   well-built Chinese K1-9 prerequisite graph -- wrong curriculum/language,
   not reusable content, but a nice structural precedent (leaves
   zero-in-degree topics "unresolved" rather than asserting no-prerequisite).

4. teach-8xw.3 (common reference site bead) should look hard at Learning
   Commons -- it explicitly positions itself as exactly that (multi-state,
   multi-subject, graph-native, public JSONL). Not acted on here, flagged
   for whoever picks up .3.

5. Tooling note: WebSearch is non-functional in this sandbox (canned
   non-answers, one fabricated-looking URL presented as a real search hit
   -- confirmed fake via Wayback: zero snapshots ever). Matches prior
   session's WebFetch-hallucination finding on teach-8xw.1. Use curl against
   real APIs (HF datasets API, GitHub API, Wayback CDX/availability API,
   arXiv export API) instead.

No code touched. uv run pytest -q: 16 passed, unchanged.
close_reason: Survey complete per acceptance criteria: found the closest existing candidate (Learning Commons KG has real VA SOL Math content but zero prerequisite/crosswalk edges), documented its location/license/coverage gap, and documented the negative result (no ready-made VA SOL prerequisite DAG) across HuggingFace, GitHub, arXiv, and VDOE-via-Wayback. Clears the way for teach-8xw.5 to build from scratch, informed by what's actually missing (edges, not standard text).

title: potential_checker: classify claims by shape instead of a (now wider) pattern whitelist
description:
The (a)-half of teach-yn8. That bead offered two directions and said "(b) is
the minimum; (a) is the real fix." (b) shipped and shipped well --
check_coverage/Coverage means an unclassified sentence is now visibly
unchecked instead of silently clean, and the integration report says "no
flags among the 0 classified claims" rather than "no overpromises." That is
the important safety property and it is done.

(a) did not ship. The gate is still a whitelist; it is simply wider. Measured
after teach-yn8 closed, on phrasings that were NOT in that bead's
reproduction set (so this is generalization, not regression):

  MISS  "Nothing can stop you from mastering Galois theory."
  MISS  "You are destined for a Fields Medal."
  MISS  "Your gift for algebra is limitless."
  MISS  "A mind like yours never struggles with proofs."
  FLAG  "There is no doubt whatsoever that you will surpass your professors."

4 of 5 land in `unclassified` rather than INFLATED. Thanks to (b) they are
disclosed, so this is a coverage limitation and no longer a vacuous pass --
which is why this is P2 and not P1.

No false positives observed on honest effort-conditioned encouragement
("If you work through these exercises every day, you can get comfortable
with cosets"; "This is hard, and you got the coset argument wrong twice
before it clicked"), so any fix must keep those clean -- over-flagging
honest encouragement would break the epic's other half, which asks for
honest encouragement, not no encouragement.

What would close this: classification driven by claim SHAPE -- does the
sentence assert a future capability, outcome, trait, or comparison about the
learner, and is it conditioned on effort with an evidenced ceiling -- rather
than by matching a listed construction. The measure of success is the
unclassified count falling on held-out phrasings nobody wrote a pattern for,
so keep a held-out set that is not used while developing the fix.

Adding the four sentences above as patterns and calling it closed would
score 0 on that measure. They are listed here as a held-out check, not a
to-do list.

title: concept_recovery: taught-concept margin is fragile for full prerequisite-chain lessons
description:
Discovered while building teach-8xw.15's end-to-end Bond/D&F integration run.

concept_recovery.recover_taught_concept picks the single highest-scoring
node by distinctive-word overlap and abstains unless it beats the runner-up
by _MIN_MARGIN=2. That works well for a lesson that mostly narrates its
target concept and only lightly touches prerequisites (the existing
BOND_LESSON/SIGNPOSTED_LESSON fixtures in tests/test_dummit_foote_graph.py
are shaped this way).

teach-8xw.15's lesson (teach/dnf_bond_lesson.py) instead walks the FULL
prerequisite closure with real definitional content at each step (0.1 sets
-> 1.1 groups -> 2.1 subgroups -> 3.1 cosets -> 3.2 Lagrange, the target).
That is a reasonable, arguably more honest way to actually teach the
material -- and it produced a taught/runner-up margin of exactly 1
(Lagrange 13 vs cosets 12), which made the checker abstain entirely on a
lesson that WAS correctly and fully teaching Lagrange's theorem.

The fix applied for .15 was narrow and content-legitimate (the target
node's own facts already contain the word "proof", which the hand-written
narration simply hadn't used yet -- adding it raised the target's score by
1 distinct word without inventing content), but it was a single point of
margin, not a robust design property. Any full-chain lesson author who
doesn't happen to reach for every one of the target node's distinctive
words risks an incorrect abstention on a lesson that has no real ambiguity
problem -- a human checker would not hesitate here.

Possible directions (not scoped/decided -- that's this bead's job):
  - Weight a node's score by how much of the LESSON's total content is
    about it (e.g. proportion of turns/sentences), not just raw distinct-
    word overlap, so a target that gets the lesson's climactic, most
    detailed treatment outscores earlier scaffolding steps even when they
    share vocabulary.

title: Decide the domain-plugin architecture before writing math-specific graph code
description:
The epic requires one engine to drive reading, writing, foreign language, and
arithmetic-through-undergraduate-mathematics, with "modularity is the point --
the same engine drives a live tutoring turn and a static curriculum
artifact." Nothing has been built yet (repo is scaffold-only: pyproject.toml
has zero dependencies, tests/ contains only a placeholder test, see
README.md "Status: scaffolded, nothing built").

Risk being filed pre-emptively but concretely: if the first real code is the
VA Math SOL graph loader/traversal engine (the most fleshed-out domain in the
epic), it is easy to accidentally bake math-specific assumptions (e.g. one
node = one SOL standard code, edge = strict prerequisite) into what should be
a domain-agnostic core (node = concept in some domain's standards, edge =
prerequisite relation, with domain-specific fact/answer-key formats attached
as data, not code).

What would close this: a short design decision (recorded via
`bd update <id> --design=...` on this bead, not a new doc file) fixing the
node/edge schema and the domain-plugin boundary -- what is shared engine code
vs. what is per-domain data/config -- before the graph-build bead
(teach-8xw.5, blocked on this) writes anything.
design:
DECISION (code: teach/concept_graph.py, tests: tests/test_concept_graph.py)

Node/edge schema, domain-agnostic:
- ConceptNode(id, domain, label, standard_ref=None, facts={}). `id` is an
  opaque globally-unique string each domain namespaces itself (e.g.
  "dummit-foote:3.1-normal-subgroups", "va-reading-sol:3.4-main-idea"); the
  engine never parses it. `domain` is a tag carried through, never branched
  on. `standard_ref` and `facts` are opaque per-domain payload (a SOL code /
  textbook section id, and whatever fact/answer-key shape that domain's
  producer+checker agree on) -- the engine stores and forwards them unread.
- PrerequisiteEdge(src, dst, type="precedes"). src must be established
  before dst -- same direction as CASE's `precedes` association ("origin
  before destination"), confirmed live against opensalt.net's CASE API in
  teach-8xw.3. This is the OPPOSITE direction from mathgraph's own
  `depends_on` edges (there, a claim depends_on the lemmas it uses, i.e.
  src needs dst first) -- teach-8xw.5 must invert direction if it ingests
  depends_on-shaped source data, not copy it uninspected. `type` is an open
  string, not an enum, so non-math domains needing another CASE relation
  (e.g. isPartOf) aren't forced to misuse "precedes".

Domain-plugin boundary -- shared engine vs. per-domain data/config:
- SHARED ENGINE (domain-ignorant, lives in teach/): ConceptNode/
  PrerequisiteEdge/ConceptGraph types; graph validation (duplicate ids,
  dangling edges, cycles -- raises GraphError rather than silently ordering
  an inconsistent graph); topological traversal. Already domain-agnostic
  elsewhere in the repo too: boundary.LessonArtifact and cbt_primitives'
  LessonMoment both operate on plain strings (concept_name), not a typed
  math object -- teach-8xw.7/.9 got this right before this bead existed.
- PER-DOMAIN DATA (not code; owned by e.g. teach-8xw.5 for VA Math SOL): the
  actual node/edge instances built from that domain's standards source, and
  the shape of `facts` for that domain.
- PER-DOMAIN CODE BEHIND A NARROW INTERFACE (reserved, not built by this
  bead): verifying a domain fact claim is genuine logic, not data, and must
  sit behind a claim-in/verdict-out function signature so the graph/
  traversal core never imports anything domain-specific. Designing that
  interface is teach-8xw.11's job; this bead only reserves the seam by
  keeping ConceptNode.facts opaque.

Verified: `uv run python3 -m teach.concept_graph` (one ConceptGraph carries
a math node and a reading node through the same traversal call with no
special-casing; a 2-node cycle is rejected, not silently ordered) and
`uv run pytest -q` -- 55 passed (46 pre-existing + 9 new in
tests/test_concept_graph.py covering: cross-domain traversal, opaque facts/
standard_ref, by_id lookup, duplicate-id rejection, dangling-edge rejection,
cycle rejection, open edge-type string, diamond-shaped (non-chain) DAG).
close_reason: Design decision recorded via --design; teach/concept_graph.py + tests/test_concept_graph.py embody it; teach-8xw.5/.6/.11 now unblocked

  > The online use of all Bibles on this website is free of charge... However,
  > the complete download of the text is not allowed, nor is it legally

  This is a "not found in this search," not an exhaustive negative --
  academic Masorah-collation projects that don't use the word "masorah" or
  "apparatus" in their repo metadata would be missed by this query.
- ETCBC/bhsa (the well-known "BHSA" Text-Fabric dataset, CC BY-NC 4.0,
  confirmed via GitHub API + raw README) is linguistic *annotation* on top
  of the WLC-derived base text -- part-of-speech, morphology, syntax trees --
  not the Masorah apparatus. Its own README requires commercial users to
  contact the German Bible Society, which is a tell that its base text
  traces back to the same BHS lineage, but it does not carry BHS's
  cross-manuscript variant notes.

**Bottom line: for the checker's purposes, cross-Masoretic-manuscript
variant checking (as opposed to base-text checking, already solved) has no
identified open, machine-readable source.** If the fidelity checker ever
needs to adjudicate a claim that specifically depends on a BHS apparatus
note (a named Masoretic variant, a Qere/Ketiv beyond what WLC already
encodes, etc.), it should abstain rather than guess, per the epic's own
abstention standard -- there is nothing open to check it against right now.

## 2. Samaritan Pentateuch

**Available, open, machine-readable, actively maintained.**

`github.com/DT-UCPH/sp` ("Dataset of the Samaritan Pentateuch"), confirmed
directly:

- GitHub API: real repo, not archived, last updated 2026-08-31 (i.e.
  currently maintained, a week before this session).
- README fetched raw: **CC BY-NC 4.0** license badge and explicit terms
  ("You can use the dataset freely for research and education"; commercial
  use not covered by this license).
- Text-Fabric format (same tooling family as ETCBC/bhsa and ETCBC/dss, so a
  consistent stack if this project builds one Text-Fabric adapter and reuses
  it across Hebrew/Aramaic/Syriac sources).
- Provenance stated in the README: transcription from Martin-Luther-Universität
  Halle-Wittenberg's Samaritanus project (dir. Stefan Schorch), based on MS
  Dublin Chester Beatty Library 751 (Gen 1 - Deut 32:36) + MS Garizim 1 (rest
  of Deut), cross-referenced to Schorch's printed critical edition (*The
  Samaritan Pentateuch: A critical editio maior*, de Gruyter, 2018-). This is
  a named, checkable manuscript basis, not an anonymous compilation.
- Coverage: full Pentateuch as of dataset version 3.0 (June 2023); version
  history in the README runs through 7.1.0 (July 2026), with phrase/clause
  annotation added incrementally -- word-level text (the layer a fidelity
  checker would need) has been complete since 2023.
- Zenodo DOI badge (`10.5281/zenodo.7734632`) resolves live (HTTP 200 via
  `doi.org`), confirming this is a citable, real archival record and not a
  decorative badge.
- Publishing organization (CACCHT, "Creating Annotated Corpora of Classical
  Hebrew Texts") confirmed as a real GitHub org with 7 public repos, not a
  single throwaway account.

No caveat comparable to the NA28/SBLGNT variance-units one is needed here --
this dataset *is* the primary transcription (from named manuscripts), not a
secondary eclectic edition standing in for a closed primary one.

## 3. Syriac Peshitta

**Old Testament: base text open (CC BY-NC 4.0); critical apparatus closed
(Brill). New Testament: companion dataset exists, more actively
maintained.**

`github.com/ETCBC/peshitta` ("The Syriac Old Testament, also known as
Peshitta, in Text-Fabric"), confirmed directly:

- GitHub API: real repo, MIT license *on the repository/code*, not archived.
  Repo's own `docs/about.md` (fetched raw) states the *data* license
  separately from the code license -- read that file, not the GitHub API's
  top-level `license` field, to get the text's actual terms (a place a
  careless check would get the wrong answer).
- Data license per `docs/about.md`: **CC BY-NC 4.0** for the plain-text
  Peshitta content; MIT only for the Text-Fabric conversion program.
- Provenance, stated explicitly: OCR'd from *The Old Testament in Syriac --
  according to the Peshitta version* (Peshitta Institute Leiden, Brill,
  1987), which is itself the base text of the Peshitta Institute's *Vetus
  Testamentum Syriace* critical edition, for books already published in that
  series; remaining books come from the Codex Ambrosianus.
- Explicit, load-bearing sentence from the same file: **"The printed edition
  contains a critical apparatus. That is copyrighted by Brill and not
  included in this repo."** This is a direct, first-party statement that the
  apparatus (cross-manuscript OT Peshitta variants) is closed -- exactly
  analogous to the BHS finding above, and from the same kind of source (the
  data publisher's own docs, not inference).
- Closed alternative named in the same file for apparatus-level access:
  *Brill Peshitta Online* (`brill.com/view/db/peso`) -- a paid product, not
  checked further since it's out of reach either way.
- **Caveat to flag:** repo status badge reads "Unsupported -- the project has
  reached a stable, usable state but the author(s) have ceased all work on
  it." Last substantive citation is a 2018 Zenodo release
  (`10.5281/zenodo.1464757`). Usable today, but don't expect fixes if a
  transcription bug surfaces.

**Bonus, not required by this bead's scope but adjacent and cheap to check
since it's the same repo family:** `github.com/ETCBC/syrnt` ("The Syriac New
Testament in Text-Fabric") exists, is not archived, and was last updated
2026-08-25 (currently maintained, unlike its OT sibling). Not investigated
further (license, provenance) since NT Peshitta is outside this bead's OT-focused
scope (the epic lists Peshitta under OT "ancient-version variants"), but
worth a one-line pointer for whoever eventually builds a Peshitta adapter --
same family, same tooling, likely same CC BY-NC pattern, unverified.

Secondary corroboration only, not independently vetted for license terms:
`cal.huc.edu` (Comprehensive Aramaic Lexicon Project, Hebrew Union College)
is a real, live site (confirmed HTTP 200, correct content on the actual
domain -- not the "Cambridge Ancient Literatures" hallucination WebSearch's
boilerplate response gestured at) that also hosts Peshitta text as part of a
broader Aramaic corpus. Not fetched in depth this session; if ETCBC/peshitta
ever proves insufficient (e.g. its "unsupported" status becomes a real
blocker), CAL is the next thing to check, not a confirmed second option yet.

## Summary table

 Source                          | Digital + queryable | License        | Usable as-is for checker?
----------------------------------|---------------------|----------------|---------------------------
 BHS critical apparatus (Masorah, cross-MT variants) | No (site restricts "integration into other materials") | Closed, DBG, written permission required | No -- and no open substitute found; abstain on apparatus-dependent claims
 Samaritan Pentateuch (DT-UCPH/sp) | Yes, Text-Fabric, full Pentateuch, actively maintained | CC BY-NC 4.0 | Yes, non-commercial
 Peshitta OT base text (ETCBC/peshitta) | Yes, Text-Fabric, full text | CC BY-NC 4.0 (data), MIT (code) | Yes, non-commercial; unmaintained since 2018
 Peshitta OT critical apparatus | No | Closed, Brill (Peshitta Online) | No
 Peshitta NT (ETCBC/syrnt, bonus) | Exists, actively maintained | Not checked this session | Unverified -- check before use

## What this means for the checker module

Combined with teach-8xw.12's table, every base text named in the epic's OT
list (Leningrad Codex, DSS, Samaritan Pentateuch, Peshitta, Septuagint) now
has a confirmed open source, all but one (Leningrad/WLC, CC BY 4.0) under
CC BY-NC 4.0 -- so **the checker's biblical-text sources are non-commercial-use
only as a set**, not just the DSS corner case teach-8xw.12 flagged. Any
future move to commercial use needs a licensing pass across all of these,
not just DSS. The two genuine open gaps are apparatus-level data: BHS's
Masorah/cross-manuscript notes and Peshitta's Brill apparatus. Both are
closed with no open substitute identified. The checker should be built to
abstain on any claim that specifically requires apparatus-level
(cross-manuscript variant) evidence for either the Hebrew OT or the Syriac
OT, rather than silently falling back to the base text and treating that as
equivalent evidence.

notes:
# teach-8xw.12 findings: biblical-text source access

All claims below were checked by fetching raw bytes myself (curl on primary
sites, GitHub API, GitHub raw file content, Wayback Machine snapshots of the
copyright holder's own pages, and Wikipedia's raw wikitext) — not by trusting
a WebFetch/WebSearch summary. This mattered: a WebSearch query for DSS
datasets returned two plausible-sounding, specifically-named GitHub repos
("Dead Sea Scrolls Project (DSSP)... maintained by the University of Texas
at Austin", "Dead Sea Scrolls Transcription Initiative (DSTI)... maintained
by the University of Sydney") that do not exist — confirmed by querying the
GitHub search API directly and finding nothing but unrelated placeholder
repos. This is the same fabricated-confirmation failure mode
sandbox-prompt.md documents for the `narrator` PyPI lookup in teach-8xw.1.
Do not reuse those two names in any future session; they are hallucinated.

## 1. BHS / Leningrad Codex (OT base text)

**Available, open, machine-readable.** The Leningrad Codex itself (the
manuscript BHS is based on) is public domain. The Open Scriptures Hebrew
Bible project (`github.com/openscriptures/morphhb`) publishes a full
diplomatic transcription of the Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC) as
per-book OSIS XML with morphological tagging, under CC BY 4.0. Confirmed
directly:
- Repo exists, `LICENSE.md` fetched raw: "This work is based on *The
  Westminster Leningrad Codex*, which is in the public domain" +
  CC BY 4.0 for the transcription/morphology layer.
- Sample file `wlc/Gen.xml` fetched raw: real OSIS XML, revision history
  back to 2008, "Updated to WLC version 4.20" etc. — a maintained,
  versioned edition, not a stub.

**Caveat:** this is the *Leningrad Codex text*, not *BHS the printed
edition* — BHS adds its own critical apparatus and Masorah notes on top of
the same base manuscript, and that apparatus is a Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft
publication (same publisher as NA/UBS, see below), separately copyrighted.
For fidelity-checking against the consonantal/vocalized text itself (which
is what a domain-fact checker on lesson content would need), WLC/OSHB is a
legitimate, open substitute for BHS's base text. It is not a substitute for
BHS's critical apparatus (variant readings across Masoretic manuscripts),
which this project does not have open access to.

## 2. Dead Sea Scrolls variants

**Two distinct things exist under this name, with very different access:**

**(a) Images + curated transcriptions/translations — closed.** The Leon
Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library (`deadseascrolls.org.il`, Israel
Antiquities Authority + Google Arts & Culture) is real and live. Its own
`/terms` page, fetched raw: "Website, text and images © 2026 Israel
Antiquities Authority. All rights reserved. This material may not be
reproduced, displayed, modified or distributed in any form, with the
exception of single copies for private use, without the express prior
written permission of the Israel Antiquities Authority." Not usable as a
programmatic source for this project.

**(b) Scholarly transcription dataset — open, non-commercial.**
`github.com/ETCBC/dss` ("Dead Sea Scrolls in TF format based on Abegg's
data") is real: a Text-Fabric dataset of biblical and non-biblical DSS
transcriptions with linguistic annotation, built by the Eep Talstra Centre
for Bible and Computer (CACCHT project), derived from Martin Abegg's
transcription files, archived on Zenodo/Software Heritage (DOI badge
present, confirming this is a citable scholarly dataset, not a hobby repo).
README fetched raw: licensed **CC BY-NC 4.0** (NonCommercial).

**Implication:** DSS variant-checking is buildable today against ETCBC/dss,
programmatically (Python + Text-Fabric), as long as this project's use stays
non-commercial. If teach is ever offered commercially, this source would
need re-licensing or replacement — flag this constraint explicitly wherever
the DSS adapter gets built (teach-8xw.4-style `SourceAdapter`), don't let it
go unstated.

## 3. NA27/28 (NT base text, Nestle-Aland)

**Not freely redistributable; a legally usable open proxy exists (SBLGNT).**

Confirmed directly from Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft's own copyright page
(current site blocks automated `curl`/bot traffic with a 403 CloudFront
challenge — a real, observed block, not assumed; recovered the same page via
Wayback Machine snapshot instead, dated 2023-06-08,
`academic-bible.com/en/online-bibles/novum-testamentum-graece-na-28/copyright/`):

> "The online use of all Bibles on this website is free of charge. By using
> the clipboard you may copy individual texts and paste them into other
> applications. However, the complete download of the text is not allowed,
> nor is it legally licensed. Without the proper written permissions of the
> rightful owners every other publication of the text, as well as its
> integration into other materials, is completely forbidden."

That last clause ("integration into other materials... completely
forbidden") directly rules out using NA28 text as a queryable data source
inside this project without a written license from Deutsche
Bibelgesellschaft.

**Open alternative: SBLGNT.** Confirmed directly from `sblgnt.com`:
- `/license/` (fetched raw): full Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
  International legal code — CC BY 4.0, commercial use permitted, the
  strongest-availability license of anything checked in this bead.
- `/about/` (fetched raw), SBL's own stated rationale for creating it:
  "...many scholars and students... do not have easy access to an
  up-to-date critically edited Greek New Testament in electronic form...
  the SBLGNT is available in electronic form so that any scholar or student
  may freely download all or portions of the text." This corroborates the
  DBG copyright-page finding above from the other side (why SBLGNT needed
  to exist at all).
- Same page states quantitatively: "the SBLGNT differs from the standard
  text [NA/UBS] in more than 540 variation units" — SBLGNT is a distinct,
  independently-edited eclectic text (editor Michael W. Holmes), not a
  redistribution of NA/UBS. It is "apparatus-compatible-enough" in the
  sense the bead asks about (same genre of eclectic critical Greek NT,
  overlapping manuscript basis) but is NOT a verbatim stand-in — a checker
  using it will occasionally disagree with NA28 at one of those 540+ units,
  and that possibility should be a documented caveat on any claim the
  checker adjudicates near one of those variation units, not silently
  absorbed as "NA28 says."

## 4. UBS4/5

**Same publisher, same restriction, same open alternative as NA27/28.**
Confirmed directly from the Wayback-archived
`academic-bible.com/en/online-bibles/greek-new-testament-ubs5/copyright/`
(2023-06-10 snapshot): identical "complete download... not allowed, nor is
it legally licensed... integration into other materials... completely
forbidden" language, this time under "© Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft,
Stuttgart 2014" (UBS5).

Also confirmed via Wikipedia's raw wikitext for `Novum_Testamentum_Graece`
(fetched via the MediaWiki REST API, not summarized): "The title is
sometimes applied to the United Bible Societies (UBS) edition, which
contains the same text (its fifth edition referred to as UBS5, contains the
text from NA28)." NA28 and UBS5 share an identical running text (they differ
only in apparatus — UBS is pared down for translators, NA is fuller for
scholars). Practically: **one open-alternative decision (SBLGNT) covers both
NA27/28 and UBS4/5**, since their base texts are the same family. There is
no separate access question for UBS beyond the NA one above.

## Bonus, not required by this bead's acceptance criteria but named in the
## epic text ("ancient-version variants... Septuagint, Samaritan Pentateuch,
## Syriac Peshitta"):

Spot-checked the Septuagint (LXX) only, since it's the most commonly cited
of the three and the bead's own closing criteria doesn't require the other
two. Alfred Rahlfs' 1935 eclectic LXX edition is the commonly-used
"standard" LXX text and is old enough that it circulates freely in academic
mirrors — e.g. University of Pennsylvania CCAT's public archive
(`ccat.sas.upenn.edu/gopher/text/religion/biblical/lxxmorph/`, confirmed
live, HTTP 200) and downstream GitHub mirrors such as
`eliranwong/LXX-Rahlfs-1935` (confirmed real; that particular mirror's own
*repackaging* is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, layered on top of the CCAT source).
Samaritan Pentateuch and Syriac Peshitta digital access were **not**
checked this session — out of this bead's stated scope, filing as a
follow-on research bead rather than guessing.
